questions.question: May you drop off a passenger for 10 seconds on crossing zig-zag lines?
options: No, stopping and parking are banned on the zig-zags
Yes, if you stay in the car
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking or waiting on crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: If you want to go straight across a box junction, what must be clear first?
options: The exit road on the far side of the box
Nothing if the light is green
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 says your exit must be clear before entering a box junction.

questions.question: Why might a cyclist wobble or swerve slightly to the right?
options: To avoid potholes, drains, or gusts of wind
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 warns that cyclists need space to avoid drains and road hazards.

questions.question: At 30 mph on a dry road, how big should your gap to the car ahead be?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 requires at least a two-second gap in dry weather.

questions.question: When should you avoid giving a signal?
options: When it could confuse or mislead other road users
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns not to give misleading signals.

questions.question: Where do street lights usually show a 30 mph limit for cars unless signs say otherwise?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 explains street-lit roads default to 30 mph unless signed.

questions.question: What light appears immediately after red and amber?
questions.explain: Rule 175: the UK traffic-light cycle is red, then red and amber, then green.

questions.question: When turning right out of a side road onto a main road, who must you give way to?
options: Traffic coming from both right and left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 requires checking and giving way to both directions when turning right.

questions.question: Who has priority at the top of the Highway Code hierarchy of road users?
questions.explain: Rule H1: pedestrians are at greatest risk and sit at the top of the road-user hierarchy.

questions.question: Before moving back to the left lane after overtaking, what must you be sure of?
options: There is plenty of room ahead of the passed vehicle
The car behind flashes its lights
You are going at least 70 mph
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 warns not to cut in front of the vehicle you overtook.

questions.question: After turning left or right into a side road, where should your car end up?
options: In the middle of the road
On the left side of that road
questions.explain: Rule 160: always finish your turn on the left side of the new road.

questions.question: When approaching a roundabout, which side should you look to first for circulating traffic?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 tells you to give way to traffic coming from your right.

questions.question: How do you signal on approach when taking the first exit to the left?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires a left signal on approach for the first exit.

questions.question: What signal must you give just before leaving any roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires a left signal as you prepare to leave a roundabout.

questions.question: In which direction do all roundabouts flow in Great Britain?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require clockwise travel on UK roundabouts.

questions.question: When the lights turn green and cyclists are inside the ASL box, what should you do?
options: Give them time and space to move off safely
Edge into the box behind them
questions.explain: Rule 178: let cyclists pull away safely and leave plenty of room when passing.

questions.question: Where must you stop when a traffic light is red?
options: In the middle of the crossroads
questions.explain: Rule 175: you must keep all of your vehicle behind the white stop line.

questions.question: On a two-lane roundabout, where should you position your car?
options: Centred cleanly inside your marked lane
Hugging the grass island on every exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to keep cleanly within their lane markings.

questions.question: Where should you stop at a STOP sign?
options: In the middle of the junction
Behind the solid white stop line
questions.explain: Rule 171: stop behind the solid white line so your car does not stick out into the main road.

questions.question: When taking the first exit on the left at a roundabout, which lane do you choose?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to approach in the left-hand lane for the first exit.

questions.question: Does a flashing amber light at a pelican crossing mean the same as a steady amber light?
options: No, flashing amber means give way to pedestrians on the crossing
questions.explain: Rule 196: at a pelican crossing, flashing amber means let any pedestrians finish crossing, then go if clear.

questions.question: What if a bus stops just before a zebra crossing to let someone cross? May you pass the bus?
options: No, you must wait behind the bus
Yes, pass slowly on the right
Yes, if you sound your horn
Only if no stripes are visible
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans passing the lead vehicle because it can hide pedestrians.

questions.question: You are turning right at a box junction. Your exit road is clear, but oncoming cars block your turn. May you wait in the box?
options: Yes, you may wait in the box to turn right
Only if you turn on hazard lights
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 makes a specific exception when turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If a large lorry is in front of you, why should you stay well back?
options: So you can see past it and its driver can see you in their mirrors
To stay in its blind spot
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 helps you stay visible and see further ahead.

questions.question: If you want to turn into a side road just past a parked car, when do you signal left?
options: After passing the parked car so nobody thinks you are stopping
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns that early signals near parked cars can mislead others.

questions.question: What does a round white sign with a black diagonal stripe mean?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 links the national speed limit sign to 60 or 70 mph limits.

questions.question: Before turning left soon after passing a cyclist, what must you check?
options: Do not overtake and immediately cut across the cyclist's path
Always turn sharply in front of them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and Rule 182 warn against 'left hooks' across cyclists.

questions.question: Does a pedestrian pelican crossing show red and amber to drivers?
options: No, it goes from red to flashing amber, then green
questions.explain: Rule 196: pelican crossings use flashing amber instead of red and amber.

questions.question: Why should you check carefully for cyclists and motorcycles at a T-junction?
options: They are narrower and easier to miss against background traffic
They must always stop for cars
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 advises looking carefully for smaller, faster two-wheelers.

questions.question: Why should you not wave a pedestrian across when stopping at a junction?
options: Another vehicle may not see them or may overtake
questions.explain: Rule H2: wait patiently without waving so the pedestrian checks for other traffic themselves.

questions.question: If the lane you want to enter has faster traffic, what should you do?
options: Pull out and let them brake
Wait for a safe gap so they do not have to slow down
Signal for one second then steer
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires waiting so faster vehicles do not have to slow down.

questions.question: If you pass a row of parked cars on your left, what should you do afterwards?
options: Return to the left when there is room
questions.explain: Rule 160: move back to the left once past the parked cars so oncoming traffic has space.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is already on the roundabout to your right and close?
options: Stop behind the give-way line and wait for a safe gap
Accelerate hard in front of it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 requires waiting until there is a safe gap.

questions.question: If you signal right on approach, which exit are you telling others you want?
options: An exit to the right (past straight ahead)
The first exit on the left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses a right approach signal for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: Why must you NEVER drive anti-clockwise around a roundabout?
options: You would drive head-on into oncoming circulating traffic
It wears out the left tyres
It is allowed only for emergency vans
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 prevents head-on collisions by keeping all traffic clockwise.

questions.question: May a motorcycle stop inside a cyclist advanced stop box on red?
options: No, motor vehicles must stop behind the first white line
questions.explain: Rule 178: the ASL box is for pedal cyclists only.

questions.question: When exiting a two-lane roundabout from the inner lane, which lane on a two-lane exit road should you join?
options: The right-hand lane of the exit road, then move left when safe
Cut straight across into the left exit lane in front of outer traffic
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps inner-lane traffic in the matching right exit lane unless clear.

questions.question: If the car ahead of you stops at a STOP line and moves off, what must you do when you reach the line?
options: Stop again at the white line yourself
questions.explain: Rule 171: every vehicle must stop at the line in turn and check both ways.

questions.question: If road arrows and signs show a different lane plan than normal, what should you follow?
options: Follow the road markings and approach signs
Always stay in the right lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to follow painted lane arrows and approach signs when marked.

questions.question: If your indicator bulb fails before a drive, what should you do?
options: Fix it before driving, or use clear arm signals if safe
Use hazard lights for every turn
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 includes arm signals when indicators are not working.

questions.question: You are in the right-hand lane of a two-lane roundabout and want to exit. What must you check before signalling left and moving out?
options: Your left mirror and blind spot for vehicles on your left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires checking left before moving across to exit.

questions.question: Are half-box junctions sometimes painted on only one side of a T-junction?
options: Yes, to keep that side clear for turning traffic
No, they are always full squares
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 covers full and half-box yellow markings at busy junctions.

questions.question: On a 50 mph rural road, why is 1.5 metres often not enough when passing a cyclist?
options: High speed creates strong air turbulence, so give even more room
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 explicitly requires even more space at speeds over 30 mph.

questions.question: At 60 mph, roughly how far does a car travel in two seconds?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 shows two seconds scales automatically with higher speed.

questions.question: Why must you watch the outer lane carefully when joining a two-lane roundabout?
options: A driver in the inner lane might switch outward or a cyclist might be riding there
The outer lane is always closed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 advises watching all circulating lanes and cyclists before entering.

questions.question: What sign sits on the central island facing approaching traffic on many roundabouts?
options: A blue sign with white keep-left arrows or white chevrons pointing left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 uses keep-left arrows and chevrons to guide traffic clockwise.

questions.question: What should you do if temporary roadworks traffic lights are stuck on red for a long time?
options: Wait and check if they are faulty before moving only with extreme care
questions.explain: Rule 176: never assume a red light is broken quickly; only proceed with extreme caution if clearly failed.

questions.question: After you have entered the exit road from a roundabout, what should you do?
options: Check your left signal has cancelled
Leave the left signal on for 300 metres
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 103 require cancelling your signal once clear.

questions.question: When you are stopped in a queue, where should you wait if space ends at a zebra crossing?
options: Before the stripes so the crossing stays clear
On top of the black and white stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 and 192 keep crossings clear for people on foot.

questions.question: If you drive down a steep hill, what must you watch to stay within the limit?
options: Your speed can creep up without pressing the accelerator
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 applies downhill too; use gears and brakes to stay legal.
